the ring-necked ducks were adversely affected by the lead shot, but that the birds did not die of lead poisoning and that there were no long-term residual effects of lead exposure.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lead toxicity in the duck is characterized by rapid onset of signs of toxicity, followed by a rapid recovery.
the ducks were able to tolerate a single lead shot in the gastrointestinal tract for a period of at least 6 weeks without any permanent effects.
the ring-necked ducks were very sensitive to the acute effects of lead, and the recovery of FEP, ALAD activity, blood lead and physical signs paralleled the recovery of the birds from lead poisoning.

the lead shot was rapidly eliminated from the blood and that the lead shot did not remain in the gastrointestinal tract of the ducks.
the effects of ingested lead on ALAD are reversible and can be monitored using this enzyme activity.
blood FEP and ALAD inhibition are not good indicators of the presence of lead in the body.
